name: Medial oblique osteotomy

card.summary: A rhinoplasty bone cut made near the midline of the nasal bones, used to reshape the bony nose and close the gap left after hump reduction.
card.note: Surgical procedure; complications include contour deformities and an open roof.

quick.overview:
A medial oblique osteotomy is a controlled cut in the nasal bones near the midline during rhinoplasty. Surgeons use it to reshape the bony vault, for example to narrow the nose or close an open roof after a bump is reduced.

The appearance payoff is a straighter, narrower or smoother nasal dorsum. It is performed by surgeons as part of nasal surgery.
quick.how: It is part of a surgical operation, done with a chisel (osteotome) or other instruments, usually together with lateral cuts that make the nasal bones mobile.
quick.risks: Surgical literature lists bleeding, loss of reduction, uneven alignment and contour deformities for osteotomies; open roof deformity is listed among rhinoplasty complications. A study examined effects on smell.

lead: A medial osteotomy is a bone cut near the midline of the nasal bones and is an integral part of most rhinoplasty procedures.[2] A medial oblique cut is a variant angled to shape the dorsum, and it is used to close an open roof, the gap that can follow bump reduction.[1][3]

In an osteotomy approach described by Clinics in Plastic Surgery, the nasal bones are treated as two thin plates released from medial and lateral attachments so surgeons can change dorsal width and the bony base independently.[4] The review also lists the usual problems with conventional cuts: bleeding, loss of reduction, hard-to-control alignment and bone spicules.[4]
A six-year series of 135 patients described using pliers for medial osteoectomy instead of chisel and hammer and reported favourable results in 98.5%, with two revisions for wide dorsums.[2]

chain: Cut near the midline of the nasal bones
Bones repositioned and open roof closed
angle.text: Surgeons use medial osteotomy to bring the nasal bones together and set dorsal width as part of rhinoplasty.[2][4]

paras: Wikipedia describes the bony part of a hump being chiselled off with an osteotome and the cut bones smoothed with rasps, then realigned.[1] A 1978 Laryngoscope paper described details such as incision placement and removing a beveled bone wedge before the medial osteotomy.[3]

Improperly performed medial osteotomy is associated with postoperative complications and contour deformities.[2] Open roof deformity appears in a list of rhinoplasty complications.[1] A 2019 study examined the effect of medial osteotomy on olfactory function after septorhinoplasty.[5]
A 135-patient case series of a pliers-based medial osteoectomy reported favourable results in 98.5%, with two revisions.[2] Other work on nasal osteotomy consists of technique reviews.[4]

timeline.event: The Laryngoscope publishes a paper on osteotomy technique in rhinoplasty.[3]
